## 1. Governance Model

### 1.1 Principles

1. **No phase begins without human approval.** Every phase gate requires written sign-off from the Delivery Lead (and Executive Sponsor for Phases 2, 5, and 6).
2. **Rollback remains valid throughout.** The legacy application must remain deployable from the current date until Phase 6 cutover is complete and validated.
3. **AI agents are drafting engines, not decision authorities.** Every agent output is reviewed by a named human before it is committed to the repository or presented to stakeholders.
4. **Issues are tracked, not hidden.** Any agent-detected issue that cannot be auto-fixed is recorded as `ISS-*` in `migration-run-journal.md` and assigned to an owner within one business day.
5. **The database is the stable anchor.** No stored procedure, table, column, or index changes are permitted during the migration programme. Any exception requires explicit Delivery Lead and DBA approval.

### 1.2 Review Cadence

| Review | Frequency | Participants | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily stand-up | Daily (working days) | Full team | Progress, blockers, ISS-* triage |
| Phase gate review | On phase completion | Delivery Lead, Architect, QA, named UAT rep | Evaluate exit criteria; sign-off or defer |
| Executive review | Fortnightly | Executive Sponsor, Delivery Lead | Programme health, budget, risks requiring escalation |
| Architecture review | On-demand, at least once per phase | Architect + both developers | Validate decisions before they are implemented |
| Production cutover review | Once before Phase 6 deployment | All team + Executive Sponsor | Final go/no-go; review Bicep what-if output |

### 1.3 Definition of "Phase Gate Passed"

A phase gate is passed when ALL of the following are true:

- All exit criteria for the phase are met (see `docs/Migration-Plan.md` per-phase exit criteria)
- CI workflow is green on the main branch
- No open `High`-severity ISS-* items related to the phase scope
- Named UAT representative has confirmed acceptance (Phases 2, 5, 6)
- Rollback procedure for the phase has been tested or reviewed

## 3. Control Mechanisms

### 3.1 Source Control

- All changes delivered via pull requests to `main`. No direct commits.
- PR must have at least one human reviewer approved before merge.
- CI must be green before merge is permitted (enforced via branch protection rule).
- Agent-generated files are committed as separate commits from human-authored changes.

### 3.2 CI Pipeline

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every PR to `main`:
- `dotnet restore` → `dotnet build` → `dotnet test`
- A failing test is a hard blocker — not a warning.
- Test failures are immediately raised as ISS-* items in `migration-run-journal.md`.

### 3.3 Migration Journal

`migration-run-journal.md` is the single source of truth for programme state:
- Every agent run is logged (Run Log table)
- Every unresolved issue is tracked (Open Issues table)
- Every architectural decision is recorded (Decision Log table)
- Token usage is recorded after each session (Token Usage table)
- The `journal-updater.agent` updates the journal automatically after every agent run.

### 3.4 Rollback Strategy (Programme Level)

The legacy `HistopathologySystem` on IIS is the rollback target for the entire programme:

| Rollback trigger | Action | Recovery time |
|---|---|---|
| Any phase 1–5 failure | Revert the affected module branch; legacy solution unchanged | < 1 hour (no deployment needed — legacy still live) |
| Phase 6 cutover failure | Swap deployment slot back to `legacy`; legacy IIS available for 5 days post-cutover | < 5 minutes (slot swap) |
| Post-cutover critical defect discovered | Slot swap to legacy + raise defect as P1; 5-day window to fix or revert permanently | < 5 minutes |

### 3.5 Database Change Control

The database is frozen for the duration of the migration programme:

- No stored procedure modifications
- No table, column, or index changes
- No new stored procedures added during the migration (reserved for post-migration phase)
- Any required SP change must be approved by Delivery Lead, Architect, and DBA — recorded in the Decision Log

### 3.6 Secret and Credential Governance

- No credentials are committed to source control at any point.
- `ISS-006` (plaintext SQL credential in `Web.config`) must be resolved in Phase 0 — a new `Web.Release.config` XDT transform must remove the credential from the production build artefact before any deployment to Azure.
- Key Vault is provisioned in Phase 6; all secrets are populated manually by the DevOps engineer with Key Vault Secrets Officer role (not by any agent or pipeline).
- MachineKey equivalents for the .NET 10 platform (Data Protection API keys) are stored in Key Vault from day one.

## 4. Human-in-the-Loop Decision Points

The following decisions **must be made by a human** — they cannot and must not be delegated to an AI agent:

| Decision point | Phase | Responsible human | If wrong, consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase gate sign-off | Each | Delivery Lead / Exec Sponsor | Phase proceeds with unresolved issues → higher downstream failure risk |
| Entra group-to-role mapping | Phase 2 | Cloud Architect + Azure admin | Wrong mapping = users see wrong pages / data |
| NT login → Entra UPN mapping strategy (ISS-009) | Phase 2 | Sr Dev 1 + DBA | GetUserByNTLogin returns wrong user or no user → authentication failure for all users |
| RMSE threshold acceptance for HistologyReport (R-002) | Phase 3 | QA + named UAT representative | Too permissive = visually different reports shipped to users |
| DataSet-to-POCO mapping decisions where column semantics are ambiguous | Phase 4 | Sr Dev 1 | Wrong POCO = silent data errors in domain logic |
| Cutover go/no-go | Phase 6 | Executive Sponsor + Delivery Lead + Architect | Premature cutover with defects in production |
| Legacy IIS decommission | Post-Phase 6 | Executive Sponsor | Decommissioning before confidence established removes rollback option |

---

## 5. Audit and Telemetry Expectations

### During migration (Phases 0–5)
- All agent runs logged in `migration-run-journal.md`
- All PRs recorded in GitHub PR history with linked ISS-* items in PR description
- CI run results retained in GitHub Actions history

### Post-cutover (Phase 6+)
- Application Insights: exception telemetry, dependency tracking, custom events for auth flow and report generation
- Serilog structured logs: warning and error events correlated by `CorrelationId` request property
- Health check endpoint `GET /health` polled every 5 minutes by Azure App Service health check probe
- Application Insights alert: trigger if exception rate exceeds 0 in first 30 minutes post-cutover, or > 5/hour in steady state
- Azure Monitor: CPU > 80% for 5+ minutes triggers alert to DevOps engineer

### Compliance note
- No PII or laboratory sample data is to be included in test data profiles used for Crystal Reports reference PDF generation (Phase 0).
- Application Insights telemetry must not include patient or sample identifiers in custom dimension properties.
